extracted.intended_audience: UC campus research administrators, development officers, and faculty considering gifts/grants from marijuana-related entities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for UC campuses on whether to accept donations, grants, or other funding from entities or individuals with direct, mixed, or indirect ties to the marijuana industry, including required due diligence and decision authority under a UC pilot program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot program: campus-level evaluation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: UC is implementing a pilot program permitting individual campuses to evaluate proposed funding from the marijuana industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the pilot, campuses are expected to evaluate proposed funding opportunities and to engage in due diligence if they are aware of or reasonably suspect that potential funding may be related to the marijuana industry. Consult UC Research Policy Analysis & Coordination (RPAC) Guidance Memo 19-02 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence and written assurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Campuses must conduct due diligence when aware or reasonably suspect that funding may be related to the marijuana industry and, in some cases, obtain written assurance regarding the source of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is access to funding from both legal activities and activities illegal under federal law, campuses must conduct due diligence and obtain written assurance that the funds provided to UC are not derived from activities illegal under federal law (including sale, distribution, or cultivation of marijuana). Campuses are advised to consider the optics of each funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1: Prohibition on accepting funding from entities directly deriving most/all funds from federally illegal marijuana activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Campuses may not accept donations, grants, or other funding from non-governmental entities or individuals that appear to directly derive all or most of their funding from conducting marijuana-related activities that are illegal under federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting funding from such an industry raises serious legal and reputational concerns. Possible risks include charges of money laundering, aiding and abetting violations of the Controlled Substances Act, federal forfeiture of assets derived from illegal activity, and reputational harm. To ensure consistency across UC, such funding is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2: Conditional acceptance for entities with separable revenue streams including federally illegal marijuana activities
rubrics_metrics.description: For entities that derive funding from separately identifiable revenue streams where one stream is from marijuana activities illegal under federal law, risks can be mitigated if the campus obtains assurance that funds flowing to the University are not derived from illegal sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to accepting funding from such entities, the campus must conduct due diligence and obtain written assurance that the funds provided are not derived from federally illegal activities (including sale, distribution, or cultivation of marijuana). Campuses should also consider potential optics of accepting such funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 3: Local discretion for entities indirectly tied to the marijuana industry
rubrics_metrics.description: For entities that are indirectly tied to the marijuana industry (e.g., companies selling legal products or services to marijuana businesses), campuses may make local decisions about whether to accept funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although legal risk of enforcement (e.g., money laundering or aiding/abetting) is lower than for Tier 1 entities, campuses may consider conducting due diligence and obtaining written assurance that funds are not derived from federally illegal activities. Campuses are also advised to evaluate the potential optics of each funding opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of legal and reputational risks (assessment factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate legal exposure and reputational impact as part of the decision whether to accept funding related to the marijuana industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit risks identified include money laundering charges, aiding and abetting Controlled Substances Act violations, risk of federal forfeiture of assets, and reputational harms. These risks inform the prohibition for Tier 1, the mitigation steps for Tier 2, and the discretionary approach for Tier 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: applies to non-governmental entities or individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance explicitly addresses non-governmental entities or individuals and categorizes them by the nature of their ties to marijuana-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three-tier framework (directly deriving most funds from illegal activities; mixed/separable revenue streams; indirect ties via providing services/products) is applied to non-governmental actors. Campus decisions and required mitigations are framed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to RPAC Guidance Memo 19-02
rubrics_metrics.description: Campus staff should consult UC Research Policy Analysis & Coordination (RPAC) Guidance Memo 19-02 for more information and implementation details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memo is cited as the authoritative source for additional guidance and procedures related to evaluating and accepting funding from marijuana-related sources.
